prompt.context: Our client, HotelOcho, is a budget hotel chain based in Spain with 800 locations across Europe, with 75% owned by franchisees and 25% owned by the company. The hotels are organized under six different brand names, which are popular among young travelers and cash-strapped business travelers alike. Though the rooms are small and spartan, the chains are renowned for bed comfort and friendly service. Customers are loyal to specific brands. HotelOcho has a highly de-centralized, hands-off management team. Over the last three years, profit has been dropping for HotelOcho. Though the industry in general has been experiencing softness and oversupply, HotelOcho's profit has been declining faster than others'. HotelOcho has hired McKinsey to help restore profitability.
prompt.question: McKinsey has determined that one of the key drivers of HotelOcho's costs is purchases of washable room items, particularly towels and bedsheets. Towels and sheets are purchased as sets (each room has one set of towels and one set of sheets) and the price of each set is negotiated at the corporate level with its supplier, which has several factories spread across Europe. When towels and sheets are ordered, the general manager of each hotel contacts HotelOcho's exclusive distributor, which orders the items from the factory and delivers them to the hotel. Can you brainstorm some ways that HotelOcho could save money on its towels and sheets orders?

clarifying_info.q: Are there different designs across brands?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, there are several designs used across brands, and not every brand (or even hotel) is consistent with its purchases. Each set costs the same, however.
No need to worry about FX (foreign exchange rates); all costs are in euros.
The distributor charges a set fee for each order placed.

clarifying_info.q: How long are towels and sheets designed to last?
clarifying_info.a: Towels and sheets are designed to last at least three years, but HotelOcho recommends replacing every two years.

clarifying_info.q: What is included in a towel set?
clarifying_info.a: A towel set includes two washcloths, three hand towels, two bath towels, and a bath mat.

clarifying_info.q: What is included in a sheet set?
clarifying_info.a: A sheet set includes four pillowcases, a fitted sheet, a top sheet, and a duvet cover.

framework: Towels and sheets (materials): use cheaper materials; include less in each set / use less material; eliminate duvet cover or top sheet from sheet set; extend replacement cycle beyond two years

Ordering process: standardize towel and sheet design across brands; coordinate buying decisions among local chains; eliminate distributor or find a new one; change supplier (e.g., move to lower-cost Chinese supplier); lock in long-term contracts for a volume discount

questions.prompt: As it turns out, the two most viable options to save money are standardization of design and moving to a Chinese supplier. Can you tell me what the savings would be in year one and year two if those changes are implemented? What are the risks associated with this strategy?
questions.guidance: Candidate should quantify the cost impact of both initiatives simultaneously. Key insight: the payback period is less than one year and by year two total cost savings exceed 20% on this key cost item. Candidate should also identify meaningful risks beyond pure cost.

math.setup: Total purchases last year: €50m. Purchase quantity: half towel sets, half sheet sets. Towels: 1.25m sets at €10 each = €12.5m. Sheets: 1.25m sets at €30 each = €37.5m. Chinese supplier discount: towels €3.00/set, sheets €5.50/set. Additional distributor shipping: towels €0.50/set, sheets €1.00/set. Net new price: towels = €10 - €3.00 + €0.50 = €7.50; sheets = €30 - €5.50 + €1.00 = €25.50. Standardization savings: 5% of €50m = €2.5m per year. One-time standardization investment: €10m.
steps: Standardization savings each year: -€2.5m → adjusted procurement = €38.75m
math.answer: Year 1 total cost: €48.75m (savings of €1.25m). Year 2+ total cost: €38.75m (savings of €11.25m, >22% reduction). Payback period less than one year.

questions.prompt: (Extra credit) We've also discovered that one-third of the franchisees are replacing their sheets and towels every year rather than every two years. Why might that be? If the necessary filters are installed, how many fewer sets will be purchased each year? How much will the company save per hotel, assuming original sheet and towel costs? Assume half of company-owned hotels and half the franchisees replace sets each year (i.e., a two-year cycle).
questions.guidance: Soft brainstorm: hard water / minerals in water diminish quality of towels and sheets, causing early replacement. Math involves identifying the number of 'always-replacers,' calculating sets saved, then computing maximum willingness to pay per hotel for a filtration system over 10 years.

math.setup: Total hotels: 800. Per the assumption, half of company-owned (0.25 × 800 = 200) and half of franchisees (0.75 × 800 = 600) replace sets each year → 200 + 300 = 500... Corrected per casebook: 200 hotels replace every year, 600 replace every other year (300 per year). Total annual purchases = 200 + 300 = 500 reference sets. The 200 always-replacers are 40% of annual purchases. 40% of 1.25m sets = 500,000 sets (each of towels and sheets). Moving to a two-year cycle saves half of those: 250,000 sets each of towels and sheets per year. Savings per year: 250,000 × €10 + 250,000 × €30 = €10m. Over 10-year system life (zero discount rate): €100m total. Per hotel: €100m / 200 hotels = €500,000.
steps: Sets saved per year: 40% × 1.25m = 500,000 sets each of towels and sheets, halved to 250,000 per set type
Max WTP per hotel: €100m / 200 hotels = €500,000 per hotel
math.answer: 250,000 fewer sets of each type per year; €10m annual savings company-wide; maximum €500,000 per hotel for the filtration system over 10 years.

brainstorming.prompt: Can you brainstorm some ways that HotelOcho could save money on its towels and sheets orders? After listing ideas, choose the best two or three to pursue first and be prepared to defend your choices.

categories.name: Materials / product design
ideas: Use cheaper raw materials (lower thread count, synthetic blend)
Include fewer items in each set (e.g., remove one hand towel)
Eliminate duvet cover or top sheet from sheet set
Reduce size of bath mat or washcloths
Extend replacement cycle from two years to three years

categories.name: Ordering process
ideas: Standardize towel and sheet design across all six brands to gain volume pricing
Coordinate bulk purchasing decisions among franchisees in the same region
Eliminate exclusive distributor or renegotiate distributor fees
Find a new, lower-cost supplier (e.g., Chinese manufacturer)
Lock in multi-year contracts to secure volume discounts
Consolidate orders to reduce per-order distributor fees

recommendation: Standardize washables design across all brands and move to a Chinese supplier; this produces >€10m in annual savings by year two with a payback period under one year
As extra credit: install water filtration systems in the ~200 hotels replacing sets annually to extend replacement cycle and capture an additional ~€10m per year in procurement savings
risks: Brand confusion and diminished differentiation between the six brands if designs are standardized
A decentralized management team may struggle to enforce standardization quickly
Political risk and quality concerns from sourcing in China
Longer transportation lead times and higher variable shipping costs
Damage to existing distributor and European supplier relationships
Water filtration system may become redundant if local governments upgrade municipal water quality
next_steps: Begin designing new standardized washables and initiate process to renegotiate or exit contract with original European supplier
Identify and qualify Chinese suppliers; pilot a small order to validate quality
Research and cost water filtration systems for high-replacement-rate hotels
